title: SDK Telemetry Snapshotter and Bootstrapping Playbook
author: Morgan Lee
body:
Overview:
This playbook describes the SDK Telemetry Snapshotter: a lightweight capture and hydrate workflow that lets developers reproduce production-like request traces, payloads, and SDK surface telemetry in local sandboxes for faster debugging and regression investigation. It covers capture policy, anonymization rules, storage lifecycle, and step-by-step bootstrapping for local and CI use.

Scope and goals:
- Provide repeatable, privacy-safe snapshots containing the minimal data necessary to reproduce client-side failures and regressions (requests, responses, timing slices, logs, SDK-level metrics).
- Make snapshots easy to create from a running environment and easy to load into developer sandboxes and CI test runs.
- Standardize retention, size limits, and access controls to meet privacy and compliance requirements.

When to use this playbook:
- Investigating non-deterministic client-side failures (timeouts, partial streams, truncated responses).
- Reproducing regressions in SDK behavior across releases.
- Creating representative test data for performance or cost-projection runs.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: DevX Observability (team lead: Priya Shah)
- Secondary contact: SDK Runtime (Evan Brooks)
- Support channel: #devx-telemetry on Slack
- Pager for production capture failures: pg-telemetry (on-call rotates weekly)

Definitions and artifacts:
- Snapshot: a compressed archive (.rdsnap) containing request/response pairs, SDK event timeline, sampled KV cache keys (hashed), and optional synthetic prompt sets.
- Capture record: metadata object (JSON) that indexes a snapshot (source_app, environment, time window, tags, anonymization_version). Example: {"source_app":"playground","env":"prod","window":"2026-02-05T14:00:00Z/2026-02-05T14:15:00Z"}.

Capture policy (recommended defaults):
- Default window: 5–15 minutes (configurable).
- Max uncompressed size: 250MB per snapshot. If size > 250MB, create sharded snapshots (suffix .partN).
- Sampling: 1:1 for flagged failures; 1:100 for routine captures.
- Anonymization: PII fields redacted per rules below.
- Retention: 90 days for production; 30 days for staging; CI snapshots expire after 14 days.

Anonymization rules (mandatory):
1. Redact any field matching regex patterns for emails, credit card numbers, SSN-like sequences, and bearer tokens. Replace with fixed tokens: <REDACTED_EMAIL>, <REDACTED_TOKEN>.
2. Hash user_identifiers with SHA256 + per-deployment salt; store salt in secure vault only accessible by DebugOps.
3. Truncate long prompts over 8k characters to first 4k + hash of remainder.
4. Do NOT capture file attachments or binary blobs.

Command-line utilities and examples:
- Capture a snapshot from a running service (prototype CLI):

```
redwood telemetry snapshot create --app-playground --env prod --window 2026-02-05T14:00:00Z/2026-02-05T14:15:00Z --reason "investigate-timeout" --tag regression-2026-02
```

- List available snapshots (filtered):

```
redwood telemetry snapshot list --app playground --env prod --tag regression-2026-02
```

- Download and load into the local dev sandbox:

```
redwood telemetry snapshot fetch --id snap-abc123 --out ./snapshots/snap-abc123.rdsnap
redwood dev load-snapshot ./snapshots/snap-abc123.rdsnap --sandbox local --apply-config local-telemetry-override.yaml
```

- Fetch snapshot metadata (JSON):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_CLI_TOKEN" https://telemetry.redwood.internal/v1/snapshots/snap-abc123/metadata
```

Bootstrapping developer sandboxes (recommended flow):
1. Create a fresh dev sandbox (or use the team's baseline VM/container).
2. Fetch the snapshot and verify the anonymization_version in metadata. Do not proceed if version mismatches and you are working with sensitive customer data; contact DebugOps.
3. Load snapshot into the local SDK mock server using redwood dev load-snapshot. The command performs:
   a. populates SDK call-response pairs into the local replay buffer.
   b. injects timeline events (latency spikes, retried calls) into the local tracing UI.
   c. configures the local telemetry sampler to replay same timing slices.
4. Run deterministic tests or reproduce the triggering scenario (follow reproduction checklist below).
5. When debugging completes, delete local snapshot files and clear sandbox secrets.

Reproduction checklist (use this when creating a snapshot for triage):
- Identify the exact time window around failure (start 30s before seen failure to 2x duration after).
- Mark relevant routes and SDK versions in capture metadata (example: sdk-js v2.4.1, host api.redwood.com).
- Annotate with a short reproduction guide in capture reason (one-liner + steps).
- Confirm anonymization applied and do a quick scan for unredacted emails or tokens.

Snapshot size, retention, and cost table:

Name | Default | Rationale
-----|---------|---------
Max snapshot size | 250MB | Keep transfers fast and sandbox loads quick
Retention (prod) | 90 days | Compliance + investigation window
Retention (staging) | 30 days | Lower sensitivity
CI snapshot TTL | 14 days | Reduce storage costs
Upload bandwidth cap | 10MB/s | Avoid saturating production egress during captures

Rollout and escalation procedure for capture failures:
1. If snapshot creation fails repeatedly (>3 attempts within 10 minutes) the local service should log an error with code SNAPSHOT_FAIL and automatically queue a reduced-scope capture (sampling-only mode).
2. The service emits an incident metric telemetry.snapshot.failure with dimensions {app, env, reason}. Alert if failure rate > 2% over 15m.
3. On alert, DebugOps triages: check bucket ACLs, KMS access to per-deployment salt, and service-side rate limits.
4. Escalate to SRE if storage errors indicate systemic capacity problems.

CI integration patterns:
- Use small representative snapshots (<= 10MB) for CI smoke tests to validate SDK upgrades and reproducers.
- Store a canonical public snapshot (fully anonymized) in git-lfs for deterministic CI runs.
- CI pipeline step (example YAML snippet):

```
steps:
  - name: Fetch snapshot
    run: redwood telemetry snapshot fetch --id snap-ci-canonical --out ./snap.rdsnap
  - name: Load for test
    run: redwood dev load-snapshot ./snap.rdsnap --sandbox ephemeral
  - name: Run regression tests
    run: npm run test:repro
```

Security and compliance notes:
- Snapshot creation requires role telemetry_creator (IAM). Only DebugOps and designated SRE engineers are granted this in production.
- All snapshots are encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys. Per-deployment salt used for hashing is stored in the Key Vault with strict RBAC.
- Access to production snapshots is audited; any access requires an incident ticket or documented investigation reason.

Troubleshooting common issues and canonical fixes:
- Failure: snapshot upload times out (ETIMEDOUT)
  Fix: reduce window length; verify egress bandwidth and retry with --bandwidth-cap. If persistent, check proxy egress rules and storage bucket ingress ACLs.
- Issue: unredacted email found in snapshot
  Fix: abort triage, rotate anonymization_version, run scrub tool: redwood telemetry scrub --id <snapshot> --rules email,token. Notify privacy@redwood.com.
- Problem: local replay shows skewed latencies
  Fix: enable local timing normalization: redwood dev load-snapshot --normalize-timings; this keeps order but scales timing to local CPU.

Best practices and conventions:
- Always include SDK version, client platform, and runtime (node/python/java) in snapshot metadata.
- Prefer small targeted snapshots over long windows. Capture multiple narrow windows if necessary.
- When saving snapshots for cross-team troubleshooting, attach a one-paragraph reproduction guide and link to the failing CI job or customer ticket.

Appendix A: Sample capture metadata (for reference)

```
{
  "id": "snap-abc123",
  "source_app": "playground",
  "env": "prod",
  "window": "2026-02-05T14:00:00Z/2026-02-05T14:05:00Z",
  "sdk": "js",
  "sdk_version": "2.4.1",
  "anonymization_version": "v2",
  "tags": ["timeout", "regression-2026-02"],
  "size_bytes": 14382745
}
```
